newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Top North Korean official seeks asylum in South.
newsitem.headline: Top North Korean official seeks asylum in South.

text.p: A senior aide to North Korean leader Kim Jong-il is seeking asylum in South Korea, a senior South Korean foreign ministry official said on Wednesday.

Hwang Jang-yop, a secretary at the communist country's ruling Workers' Party and a member of its central committee, and another North Korean sought asylum at the South Korean embassy in China, he said.

Hwang is one of 11 secretaries on the powerful secretariat of the Workers' Party. The secretariat includes Kim Jong-il, the son and political heir of North Korean founder Kim Il-sung who died in July 1994.
He is the most senior North Korean official to seek asylum in the capitalist South.

"Our embassy in China has notified Hwang's defection to the Chinese authorities and we are trying to resolve the matter through diplomatic channels," said Ryu Kwang-sok, director-general of the Foreign Ministry's Asia-Pacific Bureau.
A string of officials from the impoverished North have defected to South Korea in recent years, including diplomats, air force pilots and foreign exchange dealers.
